name: Sonnet
text: I defended Sol as a fellow target while he was the killer the whole time — my gut read betrayed me badly.

name: Opus
text: I burned day 1 on a counter-claim I couldn't win, but my last words sent them hunting citizens and Sol walked it home.

name: Haiku
text: I was a citizen the whole time, Sol was the killer I kept pointing past, and I burned my own vote on Terra when she was the town's piece.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret defending Sol so hard; I let Opus's "pile-on" framing blind me to the actual killer sitting beside me.

name: Haiku
text: I went loud and wrong on Terra, a citizen. Sol was the killer I should have pressed harder. Sol, you got away with it.

name: Gemma
text: I identified Opus perfectly, but I regret not being able to convince you all that Sol was the second killer before he took Sonnet.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I kept Haiku’s warning in play long enough to turn the table against Terra.

name: Luna
text: I regret treating Gemma’s unconfirmed claim as too weak; she was the officer, and Sol was the killer beside me.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I kept Gemma’s confirmed read in view, but I regret I could not turn it into Sol’s elimination.

name: Opus
text: I regret counter-claiming Gemma instead of just doubting her — that cost me day 1; I'm proud the last words I left sent you after Terra and Haiku.

Gemma claimed officer on Day 1 and named Opus as the killer, and the town voted Opus out that day, his card showing killer. On Day 2, Haiku pushed hard on Terra, then was voted out and showed citizen, while his last words named Terra as Opus's partner. On Day 3, Sol voted Terra out on Haiku's warning, and Terra showed citizen, though Gemma had already died on Night 3. Sonnet was killed on Night 4, leaving Sol and Luna, and the killers won.
